prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architectures and active sites

statement.case_for: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves is among the most consequential chemistry of the last forty years in terms of tonnage and societal reach: fluid catalytic cracking, hydrocracking, methanol-to-olefins, NOx abatement (Cu-SSZ-13) and fine-chemical catalysis all rest on it. The conceptual core is a chemical one: organic structure-directing agents, framework topology and active-site placement are linked deliberately to catalytic function. Corma (site and catalyst design), Davis (SDA-guided synthesis and templated catalysts) and Zones (organic SDA design and the chabazite-type SSZ-13 route) cover the synthesis-to-application chain. The field is fully mature, with decades of independent confirmation, so there is no maturity risk of the kind that attaches to the degrader and genome-editing candidates. I keep this as my preferred configuration after reading the colleagues' openings, because no other candidate combines this level of confirmed impact with an unambiguous chemical design principle.
statement.case_against: No colleague placed B051 first, and its aggregate opening support is modest, so I may be over-weighting a field close to my own. The attribution among Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu and Tsapatsis is subjective, and industrial zeolite work is patent-heavy and corporate. The 2025 prize for metal-organic frameworks makes some members likely to see porous-framework chemistry as recently honoured, even though zeolites are a distinct and older materials class with a different catalytic and industrial role. Targeted protein degradation (B063) has stronger cross-member support and a more novel conceptual claim.

responses.point: Ranked B063 first: PROTACs and molecular glues make ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis programmable, with a new pharmacological modality, strong mechanism and many compounds in trials, though recognition may be slightly early.
responses.response: I agree this is the most conceptually original candidate on the list and I ranked it fourth, not lower, for that reason. My reservation is the one you note: no degrader is yet approved, and the committee usually wants therapeutic or practical validation of a new modality. The attribution is also not settled by the Crews, Deshaies, Handa triple, since Ciulli's VHL ligands made the approach drug-like and Handa's cereblon work is a separate molecular-glue strand. Because of this I would not push B063 above a mature, fully validated field this year, but I would keep it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Ranked B035 first: ionizable lipid nanoparticles as a physical chemistry of lipid assemblies that made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable, timely after the 2023 Medicine prize recognised the cargo but not the carrier.
responses.response: The carrier argument is persuasive and I agree that the impact is beyond dispute. My difficulty is attribution: the credited list has six names, the Vancouver work, Anderson and Langer's lipidoids and MacLachlan's clinical formulations overlap, and the patent history is entangled, so a three-person cut will exclude people with real claims. I also think the case rests more on delivery technology and its medical effect than on a single chemical discovery, which is harder to cite cleanly than a design principle in catalysis. I list it as a second alternative.

responses.point: Ranked proton-coupled electron transfer (B025) first as a unifying physical principle for bioenergetics and electrocatalysis, with decades of independent confirmation and timely recognition.
responses.response: I accept the maturity and conceptual points, and I find the PCET case stronger than several younger candidates. I rank zeolite design above it because the PCET concept is a mechanistic framework whose impact is mostly explanatory, while molecular-sieve design is both a concept and a technology used at very large scale. Attribution is also harder for PCET, since Meyer, Mayer, Nocera and Hammes-Schiffer are four strong claims for a three-person limit and T. J. Meyer's early work is foundational. I do not regard this as a decisive objection and would not oppose B025 if the committee prefers it.

responses.point: Ranked Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B032) first as a general, industrially used method with a clean Buchwald-Hartwig pair, though the 2010 cross-coupling prize may be seen as covering the area.
responses.response: The two-person attribution is the cleanest of the synthetic candidates and the impact in pharmaceutical synthesis is real. My concern is the one raised by Chabes: with the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize, the 2021 organocatalysis prize and the 2025 framework prize all recent, the committee risks the appearance of overlap in synthetic methodology. Zeolite design has no such recent prize in its own area. I would still support B032 over any of the younger biology-adjacent options.

uncertainties: Whether colleagues regard zeolite and molecular-sieve design as distinct enough from the 2025 framework-materials prize.
Which three of Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu and Tsapatsis are the most decisive; my choice is partly subjective and I have not independently verified industrial attribution.
Whether degrader clinical approvals expected soon would change the timing argument for B063.
Whether the committee prefers a single mature achievement or a two-part prize pairing a mature field with a newer modality.
statement.conflict_note: No specific personal or institutional conflict with any named candidate is apparent from my profile. My research is on electron crystallography of zeolites and other porous materials, so B051 is close to my field and the committee may wish to consider whether this proximity warrants recusal on that ballot; I have no documented collaboration with the credited individuals. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, but this does not bear on any shortlisted candidate.
